question: Should QQBot permanently fail closed at 1 MiB for every inbound gateway message, or should it use a higher documented/established gateway ceiling?
rationale: The implementation mechanism is straightforward, but the exact ceiling determines whether existing valid gateway events are delivered or force a socket close; source and loopback proof do not establish that product compatibility contract.

options.title: Choose a documented or established ceiling
options.body: Set the cap to a size justified by QQBot protocol limits or an approved sibling-gateway policy and prove a near-boundary valid event plus an oversized rejection.

options.title: Accept 1 MiB as QQBot policy
options.body: Keep the proposed 1 MiB fail-closed limit and record maintainer acceptance that larger gateway events may be disconnected.

options.title: Defer the change
options.body: Leave the current behavior unchanged until QQBot event-size evidence is available.

recommendation.title: Choose a documented or established ceiling
recommendation.body: Set the cap to a size justified by QQBot protocol limits or an approved sibling-gateway policy and prove a near-boundary valid event plus an oversized rejection.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the same QQBot gateway factory and its direct/proxy transport-test pattern.
